idea-plugin.name: Taskbar Ungroup
idea-plugin.description:
Taskbar Ungroup gives every IntelliJ IDEA project window its own button on the Windows taskbar.

IntelliJ IDEA is a single-process, multi-window application: all project windows share one process-level AppUserModelID, so Windows groups them into a single taskbar button. This plugin assigns each project window a unique window-level AppUserModelID (PKEY_AppUserModel_ID) right after the project opens, which makes the taskbar show one button per project — no external helper process required.

0.3.0: optionally ungroup external applications too. Add their .exe under Settings → Tools → Taskbar Ungroup and each of their windows gets its own taskbar button. Matched by exe file name, applied via the documented Windows Shell window-property API (no process injection).

  • Applies automatically within milliseconds of a project window opening (no IDE restart needed).
  • Stable AppUserModelID derived from the project path hash — the same project always gets the same identity.
  • External applications: configure additional .exe files to ungroup their windows on the taskbar (file-name or full-path matching; real-time since 0.4.0).
  • Windows only; silently inactive on Linux/macOS.

中文说明：让每个 IntelliJ 项目窗口在 Windows 任务栏上显示为独立按钮（取消合并），同一项目标识稳定不变； 0.3.0 起可在 设置 → Tools → Taskbar Ungroup 中添加其他应用的 .exe，使其窗口也各自独立成按钮（不注入进程）； 0.4.0 起外部应用窗口实时生效（WinEvent 事件订阅）、可选完整路径匹配、兼容 2022.3 起的 IDE。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0: real-time external-window detection via an out-of-context WinEvent subscription (SetWinEventHook, EVENT_OBJECT_SHOW) delivered through the AWT message pump — new external windows are ungrouped the moment they appear instead of on the next 2-second sweep (the sweep remains as a fallback, and hook installation failure degrades gracefully to polling-only 0.3.x behavior). New optional full-path matching mode for external applications (exact install path instead of file name, eliminating same-name .exe false hits; default remains file-name matching for 0.3.x compatibility). Removing an entry now nudges affected windows (SWP_FRAMECHANGED) after clearing the AUMID so the taskbar can restore default grouping without reopening the app. Settings page warns when a JetBrains IDE executable (idea64.exe etc.) is configured as an external application, since that conflicts with per-project grouping. Compatibility range widened to 2022.3–2026.2.3 (builds 223–262, verified). Added CHANGELOG.md and unit tests for AUMID construction and matching semantics; CI now caches IDE distributions to shorten verification runs.

0.3.1 (critical fix): the AppUserModelID was written under a wrong property key (FMTID), so Windows never read it — taskbar ungrouping did not actually take effect in 0.3.0. Now writes the official PKEY_AppUserModel_ID ({9F4C2855-EE22-4C80-9C1A-1D6CE9F6D1CE}); verified end-to-end on a real Windows runner in CI (window AUMID write + independent read-back assertion for both IDE and external-app windows). Windows already carrying the ineffective key need nothing: the new key is applied on the next window/sweep.

0.3.0: new settings page (Settings → Tools → Taskbar Ungroup) — add external applications (.exe) whose windows should be ungrouped on the taskbar. Each configured application's window gets a unique window-level AppUserModelID (one taskbar button per window) via the documented Shell property API; windows are matched by exe file name and tracked in a lightweight background sweep. Removing an entry restores default grouping on a best-effort basis (reopen the app's windows to fully restore). Default behavior without any configured entries is unchanged: IDEA project windows stay grouped per project. No process injection, no helper process, no hooks.

0.2.1: all windows of the same project now share the project's identity — previously only the first window of a project was ungrouped, so a second window (Open in New Window, torn-off editor tab) fell back into the default IDE group. The post-startup fallback no longer gives up when JNA is not yet loaded (the service retries and self-heals). Window lookup now uses the frame handle directly, removing the by-title matching that could mis-apply when two projects had identical window titles.

0.2.0: first project window after IDE startup now applies the AUMID at window show time — the platform shows the frame before the project is attached to it, so the plugin polls for project attachment (150 ms) instead of waiting for startup completion.

Initial release (0.1.0): per-project window AppUserModelID with auto-apply, retry on not-yet-ready windows, and silent no-op on non-Windows systems.
